exactos.Claude Code junta instrucciones de vario:
Claude Code gathers instructions from several files:
  • ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md → personal, on YOUR machine (doesn't go into git; your team doesn't see it).
  • CLAUDE.md at the repo root → the team's, goes into git.
  • CLAUDE.local.md → personal for this repo (goes in .gitignore).
  • CLAUDE.md in subfolders → loads ONLY when Claude works with files in that folder.
  • @path/file.md inside a CLAUDE.md → imports another file (modular).
Classic question: 'a new teammate doesn't get the instructions' → they were in a personal file.
exactos.Claude elige una tool leyendo su NOMBRE,:
Claude picks a tool by reading its NAME, its DESCRIPTION and its input_schema. Nothing else.
Minimal or look-alike descriptions = unreliable selection.
A good description says: what it does, what it returns, input format, an example and WHEN NOT to use it (with the alternative). It's the first-step fix, before few-shot or a classifier.

In a multi-agent system, the subagent retries what's transient locally and only propagates to the coordinator what it couldn't resolve, with what it tried and partial results.
exactos.Compara los 3 modos. En 'plan' ningún ar: Compare the 3 modes. In 'plan' no file changes even if the agent tries: the block comes from Claude Code, not from the prompt. In 'hibrido' the change only happens after approval.

exactos.Cuando el resultado no sale como quieres:
When the result doesn't come out the way you want, the prose description is usually the problem.
  • Concrete input → output examples communicate better than adjectives.
  • TDD: write the tests first, ask for the code and share the tests that FAIL to iterate.
  • Interview pattern: for unclear tasks, ask Claude to ask you questions before implementing.
  • Related fixes → in a single message; independent ones → one at a time.
exactos.Cuando un subagente falla, el coordinato:
When a subagent fails, the coordinator needs context to decide: failure type, what was tried, partial results and alternatives.
Anti-patterns: (1) suppressing the error and returning 'no data' as a success → the report looks complete but isn't; (2) a generic 'Error' → nothing to decide with; (3) killing the whole flow because of a single failure.
The final synthesis must note the gaps: 'shipping section: incomplete due to a source failure'.

exactos.El loop agéntico: mandas el historial →:
The agentic loop: you send the history → Claude responds → if stop_reason is 'tool_use', YOUR code runs the tools and returns tool_result → repeat. You only finish when stop_reason is 'end_turn'.
Exam anti-pattern: deciding it finished because the response contains text. Claude can write 'Let me check…' AND ask for a tool in the same response.
exactos.El resultado puede variar entre corridas: The result may vary between runs. If both find everything, change the draft so the errors are subtler. Detection is by key words: read the findings to confirm.
exactos.El schema garantiza la forma; tus REGLAS:
The schema guarantees the shape; your BUSINESS RULES you validate in code. If they fail, retry sending the SPECIFIC error (which field, which value, what was expected).
Retrying works for format or structure errors; it does NOT work when the data doesn't exist in the document (the model would invent it). Pattern: extract total_declarado AND total_calculado to detect discrepancies instead of silently 'fixing' them.

exactos.En 'libre' es común un número único ('un: In 'libre' a single number ('about 3 days') without saying where it comes from is common. With provenance, the reader sees that 6 days is an old survey of 80 customers and that 2.8 is only the central zone.
exactos.En 'silencioso' el reporte suele present: In 'silencioso' the report usually presents shipping as if there were nothing to report (or omits it). With 'estructurado', the coordinator can use the partial result and say what's missing.
exactos.En CI no hay nadie que conteste: sin -p:
In CI there's nobody to answer: without -p (--print) Claude Code opens an interactive session and the job hangs.
  • -p 'prompt' → runs, prints and exits.
  • --output-format json → output your pipeline can read (result, cost, session_id).
  • --json-schema → the answer is validated against your schema (structured_output field).
  • --allowedTools, --max-turns → limit what it can do in the pipeline.
  • The reviewer must be a session INDEPENDENT from the one that wrote the code, and CLAUDE.md gives it the project context.
exactos.En conversaciones largas el historial se:
In long conversations the history gets compressed with summaries… and summaries lose what's exact: amounts, dates, order numbers, what the customer already declined.
Pattern: a 'case facts' block with the transactional data that's copied in full in every turn.
Also: trim tool results to the relevant fields, and put what matters at the start or the end (the model pays less attention to what's in the middle: 'lost in the middle').
exactos.En el examen: subagentes independientes: On the exam: independent subagents → several Task/Agent calls in the same response, so they run in parallel. Change D13_PARALELO to False and compare the total time.
exactos.En la API actual usa Haiku 5.5 para esta: In today's API use Haiku 5.5 for this part, or auto + a clear instruction + strict: true.
exactos.En modo 'solo_prompt' no hay nada en el: In 'solo_prompt' mode there's nothing in the code to stop it: it would run without asking.
exactos.En sesiones largas de exploración el con:
In long exploration sessions the context fills up and the agent starts giving generic answers or answers inconsistent with what it had already found (context degradation).
Patterns: (1) a scratchpad file where the agent notes key findings; (2) subagents for exploring, which return only a summary; (3) /compact; (4) a new session + summary instead of dragging everything along.
exactos.En «caido», el genérico devuelve una lis: In «caido», the generic one returns an empty list with no error: Claude has no way of knowing the system failed. The structured one says what happened (errorCategory), whether retrying helps (isRetryable) and what to do (description).

exactos.Escala cuando: (1) el cliente lo pide ex:
Escalate when: (1) the customer explicitly asks for it, (2) the policy doesn't cover the case, (3) you can't make progress.
These are NOT good triggers: sentiment by itself, or the 'confidence' the model claims to have.
Ambiguity: if there are several possible customers, ask for one more piece of data; never pick with a heuristic.

exactos.Few-shot = incluir 2 a 4 ejemplos de ent:
Few-shot = including 2 to 4 input → output examples in the prompt. It's the most effective technique when instructions alone give inconsistent results.
The best examples cover the AMBIGUOUS cases and explain WHY it was decided that way; that way the model generalizes the criterion and doesn't just copy the format.

exactos.Grep = buscar DENTRO de archivos (¿quién:
Grep = search INSIDE files (who calls processRefund?).
Glob = search for files by NAME or path (which ones are the *.test.ts?).
Read = read a file.  Edit = targeted change with unique text (if it isn't unique, it fails → Read + Write).
Incremental exploration: first Grep to find entry points, then Read to follow imports (like the processRefund → submitRefund re-export). Reading the whole repo at once wastes context.
exactos.Instancia nueva: no vio cómo se escribió: New instance: it didn't see how the draft was written.
exactos.Instrucciones vagas ('marca lo important:
Vague instructions ('flag what matters', 'be conservative', 'only if you're highly confident') leave the model guessing where the line is. Result: false positives (too many alerts) or false negatives.
Fix: concrete criteria for what DOES and what DOESN'T count, with examples. False positives destroy trust in the WHOLE system, even in the correct alerts.

exactos.Llega un documento y no sabes si es fact:
A document arrives and you don't know whether it's an invoice, a receipt or a contract. You have one schema (one tool) per type.
  1. forced tool (extraer_metadatos) → guarantees that step goes FIRST.

exactos.MCP (Model Context Protocol) estandariza:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) standardizes how an agent discovers and uses external tools and data.
  • Tools = actions Claude can call.  • Resources = data that can be read (catalogs, docs).
  • A stdio server runs as a subprocess; Claude Code / the Agent SDK start it.
  • In Claude, MCP tools are called mcp__<server>__<tool>.
  • Configuration: .mcp.json in the repo (shared with the team, goes into git) or ~/.claude.json (personal). Secrets go in as ${VARIABLE}, never written in the file.
exactos.Matemáticas de SLA: si el reporte debe e: SLA math: if the report must be ready at 8:00 and the batch can take up to 24 h, you have to send it by 8:00 the day before at the latest (or split the work into shorter windows).
exactos.Message Batches API: mandas muchas petic:
Message Batches API: you send many requests together and it processes them asynchronously.
  • It costs ~50% less.  • It can take up to 24 h (no latency SLA).
  • Each request carries a custom_id to match results.  • There's no tool loop inside the batch (each request is single-turn).
Use it for what can wait (nightly reports, audits). NOT for what blocks someone (a review before a merge).

Asking for 'answer only in JSON' in the prompt works almost always… and 'almost' breaks a pipeline: sometimes it arrives with ```json, with a sentence before it, or with fields added or missing.
tool_use with input_schema + forced tool_choice = the JSON is always parseable and follows the schema.
Schema design: optional fields as nullable (so it doesn't invent), enum with 'otro' + detail.
Careful: the schema guarantees the SYNTAX, not the SEMANTICS (a total may not add up → demo 4.4).
exactos.Plan mode = Claude explora y propone un:

Use it when the task is AMBIGUOUS: there are several valid ways to do it and it's worth choosing before editing.
Plan mode: large changes, with several valid approaches or architectural ones. Direct: a clear, well-scoped change.
Hybrid pattern: plan → review/approve → execute.

exactos.Un 97% de precisión global puede esconde:
A 97% overall accuracy can hide a category that fails much more.
  • Measure accuracy BY document TYPE (and by field) before removing human review.
  • Stratified sampling: review a sample of each type, not just of the total.
  • Ask for per-field confidence and CALIBRATE it with labeled data: decide the threshold with evidence.
  • Low confidence → human review queue.
exactos.Un coordinator descompone la tarea, dele:
A coordinator decomposes the task, delegates each subtopic to a subagent and then synthesizes. All communication goes through the coordinator. Each subagent starts with an empty context.
Classic question: if the final report is missing a whole topic, the cause is usually the coordinator's decomposition, not the subagents.
exactos.Un error genérico ('Operation failed') n:
A generic error ('Operation failed') doesn't tell Claude whether to retry, ask for other data or escalate. Worse: returning an empty list when the system failed makes Claude say something FALSE ('you have no orders').
Structured error = is_error: true + errorCategory (transient / validation / business / permission) + isRetryable + a readable description. And a valid empty result is NOT an error.
In MCP the field is called isError in the tool's result; in the Messages API it's is_error in the tool_result block. Same idea.
exactos.Un modelo que revisa su propio trabajo e:
A model that reviews its own work in the SAME conversation carries over the reasoning that got it there: it tends to confirm instead of question.
An INDEPENDENT instance (without the generation history) that only sees policy + case + result finds more problems.
Also: ask for confidence per finding and send the low-confidence ones to human review.
